description: R08 TerminalSettingsTests checkpoint: safe Rust owns binding-to-NewTerminalArgs projection, profile/default composition, color-scheme layering, title promotion and launch-position parsing. Six contracts are Exact; CommandLineToArgvW, NormalizeCommandLine and command-line profile matching are Partial only for their native argv memory layout or Win32 environment/SearchPath/filesystem adapter.

entries.notes: Rust reproduces all twelve ctrl+a..l binding vectors, split directions, NewTerminalArgs payloads, explicit/generated profile selection, defaults fallback and TerminalSettings commandline/title/directory/history composition.

Rust owns Windows command-line argument value and quoting semantics across 1..16 arguments. Microsoft's additional assertion that CommandLineToArgvW returns argv strings contiguously inside one HLOCAL block is a native API memory-layout property, not portable product behavior.

Rust owns tokenization, progressive unquoted executable-candidate reconstruction, canonical executable substitution and NUL-separated argument projection. Environment expansion and SearchPath/filesystem canonicalization are injected through CommandLinePlatform rather than Win32.

Rust reproduces all nine Microsoft vectors: case-insensitive longest-prefix selection, connectionType exclusion, invalid-path preservation and profiles.defaults fallback. Production executable/environment normalization remains delegated to the classified CommandLinePlatform seam.
CreateWithProfile preserves each profile history size and CreateWithNewTerminalArgs(null) resolves the configured default profile.
Validation retains two active profiles, records the two native warning observables, retargets the effective default to profile zero and successfully composes historySize=1.
Rust applies scheme cursor color first and then profile cursorColor, reproducing all six Microsoft scheme/profile/default precedence vectors.
Rust reproduces profile/title precedence and the exact quoted, unquoted, empty-first-component and leading-space command-line title promotion vectors.
LaunchPosition parsing reproduces single-value duplication, one-sided comma values, paired values and invalid-token omission for all six Microsoft vectors.
